questions.question: In a 2nd-order IIR Notch filter designed for 50 Hz cancellation, what is the effect of increasing the Quality Factor (Q)?

answers.a: The notch bandwidth becomes narrower, preserving adjacent ECG frequency components
answers.b: The notch bandwidth widens, attenuating the entire ECG spectrum
answers.c: The sampling rate of the system is halved
answers.d: The filter turns into an ideal high-pass differentiator

explanations.a: Because Q = f0 / BW, a higher Q decreases bandwidth BW, producing a sharp notch that eliminates 50 Hz without clipping QRS or P-wave diagnostics.
explanations.b: Lower Q widens the notch bandwidth, not higher Q.
explanations.c: Quality factor does not alter the hardware sampling frequency.
explanations.d: Q-factor adjusts the pole radius in the z-plane, maintaining a bandstop notch characteristic.

questions.question: What is the expected Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) of a modern galvanically isolated biomedical front-end?

explanations.a: A CMRR of < 20 dB would leave severe common mode distortion.
explanations.b: Non-isolated standard operational amplifiers offer 60-80 dB CMRR.
explanations.c: With an optical/capacitive galvanic isolation barrier breaking ground loops, CMRR routinely exceeds 110 dB to 120 dB, eliminating mains hum.
explanations.d: 0 dB represents unity gain with zero common mode rejection.
